entities.summary: Alan Charles Jardine is an American musician who co-founded the Beach Boys. He is best known as the band's rhythm guitarist, background vocalist, and for occasionally singing lead vocals on singles such as number-one hit "Help Me, Rhonda" (1965), "Then I Kissed Her" (1965), "Cottonfields" (1970), and a cover of the Del-Vikings' "Come Go with Me" (1981). His song "Lady Lynda" was also a UK top 10 hit for the group in 1979. Other Beach Boys songs that feature Jardine on lead include "I Know There's an Answer" (1966), "Vegetables" (1967), a cover of Buddy Holly's "Peggy Sue" (1978), and "From There to Back Again" (2012).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a founding member of the Beach Boys, Al Jardine contributed to the band's success with hits like 'Help Me, Rhonda' and 'Lady Lynda', which reached the top 10 in the UK. His work helped shape the sound of American popular music in the 1960s.
